title: Internal LB failover & telemetry — terraform module for hybrid NLB/ALB ingress with health sentinel
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that implements an internal ingress pattern combining NLB for TCP passthrough and ALB for TLS termination and HTTP health probing. The module must support zero-downtime upgrades, cross-AZ failover, certificate rotation hooks (KMS/HSM integration handled by infra ops), and an active 'health sentinel' that verifies both L4 connectivity and in-cluster app readiness before advertising targets to upstream routing. The goal is to make Private (VPC) deployments resilient to instance drains, control-plane upgrades, and to surface deterministic health signals to the Redwood Console.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Terraform module (module.internal_ingress) published in git://infra/terraform-modules with documented inputs/outputs; 2) Deployments in staging show NLB TCP passthrough -> ALB TLS offload optional path; 3) Health sentinel correctly marks targets unhealthy when either TCP probe fails or application readiness endpoint returns non-2xx; 4) Certificate rotation can be triggered via a module variable and performs in-place ALB certificate swap without traffic loss; 5) Canary upgrade runbook documented and executed in staging with bake period and rollback guard; 6) Module exposes telemetry: last_health_cycle, failure_count, last_rotate_timestamp tags on targets.
decisions:
- Use hybrid model: NLB targets ELB TCP passthrough for low-latency protocols (gRPC/HTTP2) and route web traffic through ALB when TLS termination is desired.
- Health sentinel will run as a sidecar on each target ASG instance and will call both TCP connect to local listener and an application /_probe/ready HTTP endpoint; both must pass for target to be marked healthy.
- Connection draining: use AWS target group slow drain (300s) and add a post-drain 'kv-warm' check to ensure KV cache has checkpointed; drain then deregister.
- For cert rotation we will create a two-step swap: create new certificate listener, warm backend weights to 0->1, then de-register old listener. This avoids a global restart.
- Metrics will be exposed to CloudWatch and Redwood Console via the existing metrics sink (namespace: redwood.internal_ingress).
tech_notes: Terraform module will accept variables: vpc_id, private_subnets, internal_nlb_subnets, alb_subnets, enable_alb_tls (bool), alb_certificate_arn, health_sentinel_image, sentinel_pull_policy, target_group_port, target_protocol, connection_draining_timeout. Outputs: nlb_dns, alb_dns, target_group_arn, health_sentinel_iam_role_arn. Implementation touches: aws_lb, aws_lb_target_group, aws_lb_listener, aws_lb_target_group_attachment, aws_ecs_service/ASG lifecycle hooks (optional). Use lifecycle "prevent_destroy" on critical resources during upgrades and add a module var allow_force_destroy=false by default.
test_plan:
- Unit: terraform validate and plan with example vars (localstack or aws-vcr for plan).
- Integration: deploy to staging VPC with 3 AZs. Run these tests: TCP connect to NLB endpoint, HTTPS request to ALB when TLS enabled, simulate app readiness failing and assert target becomes unhealthy in ALB.
- Chaos: simulate instance termination during in-flight requests and verify connection draining + ALB failover with no 5xx spike above SLO.
- Cert rotation test: rotate a cert in staging and verify 0 downtime and correct metrics emitted.
- Security: run module through internal static checks and require IAM role least privilege review.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge module to monorepo under modules/internal_ingress, tag v0.1.0.
2) Deploy module in a noncritical staging cluster.
3) Run canary on a small service team for 48h with alerting enabled.
4) If metrics stable, roll to larger fleet with 30m bake windows and automated rollback on error budget breach.
5) Post-rollout: retro and refine drain timeouts and sentinel thresholds.
